data.question: CNC-02 spindle alarm SP-104, grinding noise
data.summary: Spindle bearing wear is the most likely cause of CNC-02’s SP-104 alarm and grinding noise. Check spindle vibration and bearing temperature from the HMI first.

citations.quote: worn spindle bearings (most likely)
blocked coolant filter (possible)

fix.title: Replace spindle bearing set
steps: Stop the machine, apply lockout and tagout on the main isolator, and verify zero energy.
Remove the spindle cover and disconnect the drawbar and coolant lines.
Extract the spindle cartridge with the puller and mount it on the bench.
Press out both bearings and fit the new BRG-7014-ACD pair with the spacer.
Fit a new SEAL-SPDL-70 front seal and pack the bearings with GREASE-KLB-2.
Refit the cartridge, run the 20-minute warm-up cycle and check that vibration is below 2.5 mm/s.

citations.quote: Plant ref: PROC-CNC-01 | Lockout required: yes | Time: 240 min
(plant ref PROC-CNC-01)

other_fixes.title: Check spindle vibration from the HMI
steps: Open Diagnostics, then Spindle, on the HMI and start the vibration test at 6000 rpm.
Record the vibration reading and the bearing temperature.
If vibration is above 2.5 mm/s or the temperature is above 65 C, plan PROC-CNC-01.
Log the readings in the shift handover.

citations.quote: Plant ref: PROC-CNC-02 | Lockout required: no | Time: 20 min
(plant ref PROC-CNC-02)

other_fixes.title: Clean coolant filter and flush lines
steps: Stop the coolant pump and apply lockout and tagout on the coolant pump breaker.
Drain the filter housing into the waste tray.
Replace the filter element with FLT-CL-25 and clean the housing.
Flush the lines at low pressure for 5 minutes and check for leaks.
Remove the lockout, restart the pump and confirm pressure above 18 bar.

claims.text: SP-104 indicates high spindle temperature, with worn spindle bearings listed as the most likely cause.
Past spindle-bearing breakdowns also involved grinding noise and a vibration alarm.
The manual directs an HMI spindle vibration check that records vibration and bearing temperature.
A blocked coolant filter is an alternative cause of SP-104; the manual associates it with dropping coolant pressure and hot parts.

4.2 Check spindle vibration from the HMI
Plant ref: PROC-CNC-02 | Lockout required: no | Time: 20 min
No isolation needed. Work from the HMI only.
1. Open Diagnostics, then Spindle, on the HMI and start the vibration test at 6000 rpm.
2. Record the vibration reading and the bearing temperature.
3. If vibration is above 2.5 mm/s or the temperature is above 65 C, plan PROC-CNC-01.
4. Log the readings in the shift handover.
Parts required: none.
